name: Syndromic Microphthalmia-Anophthalmia-Coloboma

criteria.description: Presence of microphthalmia, anophthalmia, or coloboma confirmed by clinical examination or imaging
Presence of at least one systemic anomaly such as craniofacial dysmorphism, neurological abnormalities, or skeletal defects
Identification of pathogenic variant in known MAC-associated genes (e.g., SOX2, OTX2, PAX6)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least two major criteria including ocular malformations and systemic anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.

searchTerms: one or both eyes abnormally small

pathognomonic.symptomName: Coloboma of the iris, retina, or optic nerve
searchTerms: missing part of iris or retina
hole or gap in eye structures
defect in colored part or retina of eye

pathognomonic.symptomName: Anophthalmia (complete absence of one or both eyes)

common.symptomName: Craniofacial dysmorphism including micrognathia and midface hypoplasia
searchTerms: small lower jaw and flat midface

common.symptomName: Hypoplasia or agenesis of the optic nerve
searchTerms: poorly formed nerve connecting eye to brain
optic nerve absence or small size

occasional.symptomName: Skeletal anomalies such as clinodactyly or syndactyly

rare.symptomName: Renal malformations including renal agenesis or hypoplasia
Endocrine abnormalities such as growth hormone deficiency

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; genetic testing for MAC-associated gene mutations
imaging: Orbital ultrasound or MRI showing microphthalmia or anophthalmia
Brain MRI may reveal associated structural abnormalities
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SOX2, OTX2, PAX6, or other MAC-associated genes
other: Ophthalmological examination confirming coloboma and optic nerve anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: Negative genetic findings for syndromic MAC genes
Predominantly ocular involvement without microphthalmia or anophthalmia

redFlags: Complete bilateral anophthalmia with severe developmental delay
Presence of multiple congenital anomalies including cardiac and renal defects
Seizures or neurological deterioration in infancy
references: Verma AS, FitzPatrick DR. Anophthalmia and microphthalmia. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2007;2:47.
Schimmenti LA, et al. Genetic basis of microphthalmia and anophthalmia. Am J Med Genet C Semin Med Genet. 2005;137C(1):38-44.
